provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
In the original task, a block two cells wide runs down the rows (lane direction +row). It is drawn on a square grid with background 7. Starting from the top row, the rows alternate between the reference pair (A,B) and the swapped pair (B,A). Every row that differs from the top row is shifted one cell to the right (+col). The factory pushes the lane vector (1,0) and the shift vector (0,1) through the D4 transform. A reflection negates the column component, and each clockwise rotation maps (dr,dc) to (dc,-dr). The background constant becomes palette[7].

The emitted program works directly in visible coordinates:
1. It finds the bounding box of all non-background cells.
2. It decides whether lanes are rows or columns from the transformed lane vector.
3. It takes the reference lane at the start end of the lane direction. That is the box edge opposite the lane vector, the image of the original top row.
4. Every lane whose segment differs from the reference lane is cleared to background and redrawn one cell along the transformed shift vector, clipped to the grid.

The reference end matters when the block length is even, because the two end lanes then differ. That is why the reference end is fixed by D4 rather than guessed. The code was not executed; this mechanism is a hand-check against the approved fixtures under d4=0.
draft_notes.limitations:
No tests have been run. The background is fixed as the constant palette[7] rather than inferred as the most common colour. This is safe for this constructor: 7 is never a pattern colour, and even when the block is large, the most-common count would only tie and never be beaten.

The program assumes the constructor's domain: a single alternating block two cells wide, with room to shift (the constructor keeps col <= size-3). Out-of-bounds shifted cells are clipped, which never happens for valid generated scenes. Demonstrations are not consulted, because the geometry is fully determined by d4 and palette.

No constructor defects or fixture contradictions were found. The fixtures match the generator and the uniform rule.
